tier1.text: A small organelle enclosed by a single membrane, and found in most eukaryotic cells. Contains peroxidases and other enzymes involved in a variety of metabolic processes including free radical detoxification, lipid catabolism and biosynthesis, and hydrogen peroxide metabolism.
tier1.attribution: Definition from the Gene Ontology (GO 2026-07-26), GO:0005777. CC BY 4.0.

figures.title: Peroxisomes: ABCD3 immunofluorescence
figures.caption: Cultured human cells (A-431) stained by immunofluorescence for the ABCD3 protein (green), which HPA locates only in the peroxisomes (reliability enhanced). Other colours are reference stains (blue: nucleus; red: microtubules).
figures.alt: Fluorescence microscope image of cells with ABCD3 protein in green, marking the peroxisomes.
figures.credit: Image from the Human Protein Atlas 25.1 (proteinatlas.org): Peroxisomes: ABCD3 immunofluorescence, https://images.proteinatlas.org/32026/570_F10_2_blue_red_green.jpg. CC BY 4.0.

figures.title: Peroxisome
figures.caption: Peroxisomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain an abundance of enzymes for detoxifying harmful substances and lipid metabolism.
figures.alt: This diagram shows a peroxisome, which is a vesicular structure with a lipid bilayer on the outside and a crystalline core on the inside.
figures.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
